### [1:40–3:10] STEP 1 — PICK THE ONE JOB  (the GOAL)
**NARRATION:** "Step one: pick the job. This is the 'goal' in the formula, and the biggest mistake
is going too big. Don't build an agent to 'run marketing.' Build one to do a single, repeatable job
with a clear finish line. Good first jobs: answer a common customer email, turn a voicemail into a
tidy summary, qualify a new lead, or draft a first-response quote. Pick one where you'd know a good
result the instant you saw it."
**[VISUAL]:** A shortlist of 4 starter jobs appears; a cursor circles **"Answer common customer
emails."**
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "A great first agent does one narrow job you already understand — not a
vague job you're hoping it'll figure out."

### [3:10–4:50] STEP 2 — BUILD THE BRAIN IN MINDSTUDIO  (the INSTRUCTIONS)
**NARRATION:** "Step two: build the brain. Go to MindStudio, start a new agent, and write its
instructions in plain English — like you're training a new hire on day one. Tell it who it is, what
job it's doing, the steps to follow, and the rules it must never break. Under the hood it runs on a
model like Google Gemini, but you never touch that — you just write the instructions. And be
specific. 'Be friendly' is weak. 'Answer in three sentences, never promise a refund, and if you're
unsure, hand it to a human' — that, it can actually follow."
**[VISUAL]:** MindStudio editor on screen: type an instruction block — **Role · Steps · Rules.**
Model dropdown shows **Google Gemini.**

### [5:35–7:05] STEP 3 — GIVE IT A TOOL  (the TOOLS)
**NARRATION:** "Step three: give it a tool. Right now your agent can think, but it can't do. Tools
are what let it act in the real world — read your inbox, look something up, add a row to a sheet,
draft a reply. In MindStudio you add these with a click. Start with one. Just one. If your agent
answers customer emails, give it your FAQ document, so its answers are actually right instead of
made up. Add tools the way you'd hand a new employee keys — one at a time, only what the job needs."
**[VISUAL]:** MindStudio 'Add tool' panel; connect a single tool — a knowledge doc — and toggle it
**ON.**
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Instructions give your agent judgment. Tools give it hands. It needs
both to be useful."

### [7:05–8:25] STEP 4 — TEST IT, THEN DEPLOY  (the test everyone skips)
**NARRATION:** "Step four: test it, then deploy — and do not skip the test. Before this thing
touches a real customer, run it on ten examples yourself. Feed it questions you already know the
right answer to, and watch what it does. Here's the one test every agent must pass: when it doesn't
know, does it hand off to a human — or does it make something up? If it guesses, tighten the
instructions and test again. Once it passes, deploy it — publish it as a link, drop it on your
site, or connect it to your inbox. Now it's working while you're not."
**[VISUAL]:** Run 3 test prompts — one it nails, one it correctly hands off to a human — then hit
